column1: # EVENTS-NONE.tsv -- an entry of ipl_gprogs that waits for an event and is NOT graded on a script of its own work, because that work is not the same on two runs of the graphics oracle within the road's law (row icon-graphics-the-waiting-gprogs-do-their-own-work-half-a and -half-b, the cto 2026-11-16): entry, a tab, the measured reason. Such an entry keeps its still picture as its answer.

column2: MEASURED officer_02 2026-11-16 on icon-master-x through the screen road: every line of its standard output begins with &interval, the X server milliseconds since the last event, and carries it again in the high bits of the event word (two runs of one script: 3541 and 3570 ms, 50 and 51 ms); masking those lines would mask the majority of the answer, so it keeps its still picture

MEASURED officer_02 2026-11-16 on icon-master-x through the screen road: initialize() calls randomize(), so the deck is dealt from the clock and two runs of one script turn up different cards (the census: events DIFFERS); it has no option that takes a seed, and the pin (NAME.pin) is laid over the whole road, whose own still rule it freezes: two runs of concen under the shim on util_screen_run.py each read screen unstable. It keeps its still picture

MEASURED officer_02 2026-11-16 on icon-master-x through the screen road: report() writes each action's CPU seconds (&time - lastclk) on its status line and on standard output; one script of seven clicked points and I N G T U L Q, run twice, reads 0.00 sec and 0.01 sec for 2-opt and uncross, screen and text alike; no option hides the status line. It keeps its still picture

MEASURED officer_02 2026-11-16 on icon-master-x through the screen road: main() calls randomize() and the chaos game draws without end while it runs; one script (G, S, 4, G, S, q) read screen unstable at the road's 30 s on the first run and gave six lines on the second; the vertex colour of a pixel is the last random draw to land on it. It keeps its still picture

MEASURED officer_02 2026-11-16 on icon-master-x through the screen road: main() calls randomize() and every colour the program allocates, fixed or mutable, is ?65535 of each channel; one script (f, F, q) gives the same first picture and two different second and third pictures on two runs. It keeps its still picture

MEASURED officer_08 2026-11-16 on icon-master-x through the screen road: its own work is a file chosen in its navigator (navitrix), whose window names the run's own folder as its title and lists that folder's files; the folder differs between the oracle's cut and the graded run (two cuts read DIFFERS on the screen at the navigator), and the navigator has no field to name another folder, nor a fixed number of ../ steps out of it, so it keeps its still picture

MEASURED officer_08 2026-11-16 on icon-master-x: it plots only the coordinate files *.crd of its own working folder, listed at its start (filelist("*.crd")); the graded run's folder holds none, so its plot, scale and offset change nothing that can be seen, and it keeps its still picture

MEASURED officer_08 2026-11-16 on icon-master-x through the screen road: it calls randomize() and, once its pause button is released, draws without end; the road reads screen unstable on the oracle, an answer no ref carries, so it keeps its still picture (paused at its start)

MEASURED officer_08 2026-11-16 on icon-master-x: it recolours an image through mutable colours, and NewColor fails on the road's 24-bit display (fixtures/icon_xwin of harness, xwin_colours answers NewColor failed), so opening any image ends at its notice Cannot get mutable color.; it keeps its still picture

MEASURED officer_01 2026-11-16 on icon-master-x through the screen road: scroller reads no event (its text calls no Event, WDone, WQuit or Active; it loops CopyArea and WDelay(10) for ever and only the road ends it), so no script can do or end its work; its work is the scroll itself, which never holds still on an image that differs across its columns (small.gif, 24x16: screen unstable within a 60 s cap), so it is graded on bands.gif, horizontal bands that scroll onto themselves, its picture still.
